title: The Americas

hook.deadpan: 1775. Most of the Americas is ruled from Europe. Not for long.
hook.epic: Fifty years. A hemisphere breaks free.

beats: Lexington & Concord
Shots at Lexington. Nobody agrees who fired first.
Lexington and Concord: the war for American independence begins.
Declaration of Independence
Thirteen colonies declare independence. Britain declines.
1776: the United States declares independence.
Yorktown
Cornwallis surrenders at Yorktown. Britain gives up on the colonies.
Yorktown: the war for independence is won.
Bois Caïman uprising
In Saint-Domingue, the enslaved rise up.
1791: the Haitian Revolution begins.
Haiti independent
Haiti beats Napoleon's army and declares independence.
1804: Haiti, the first free Black republic.
May Revolution
Napoleon holds Spain's king. Buenos Aires decides it can rule itself.
1810: Buenos Aires removes the viceroy.
Grito de Dolores
A priest rings a church bell. Mexico's war of independence starts.
The Cry of Dolores: Mexico rises.
Chacabuco
San Martín marches an army over the Andes.
Chacabuco: San Martín crosses the Andes and frees Chile.
Boyacá
Bolívar crosses the Andes too. In the rainy season.
Boyacá: Bolívar liberates New Granada.
Army of the Three Guarantees enters Mexico City
Mexico becomes independent. Briefly, it has an emperor.
1821: Mexico wins its independence.
Cry of Ipiranga
Brazil's prince declares independence from his own father.
1822: Brazil breaks from Portugal.
Ayacucho
Spain's last army in South America surrenders.
Ayacucho: Spanish rule on the mainland ends.
end_card: Every year. Every border. Explore it yourself.
